title: Accounting and Finance Policies and Procedures
overview: Accounting and finance policies and procedures are crucial for implementing effective internal control systems across an organization. They play a significant role in every business cycle, including purchasing and payments, inventory and production, HR and payroll, fixed assets and capitalization, and the sales and collection processes.

These policies and procedures are indispensable tools for boards of directors and senior management to define and communicate the limitations and authorities assigned to various managers and employees. Additionally, they are essential for organizing financial reporting and ensuring compliance with external regulatory requirements.

This course encourages participants to adopt risk-based approaches for creating and implementing operational policies and procedures. Participants will learn to allocate tasks efficiently using proper segregation of duties and to leverage software for effective control implementation. The course also includes an overview of sample financial statements aligned with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).
audience: This course is designed for accounting and finance professionals seeking to enhance their skills in designing and implementing robust financial policies and procedures.
methodology: The course employs a mix of expert-led discussions, practical exercises, and group work. Participants will learn how to write and structure policies and procedures for different business cycles and align financial reporting with IFRS requirements.
competencies: Allocating and segregating tasks among employees.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Develop and design a comprehensive accounting and finance manual.
Plan the necessary resources for the accounting and finance department.
Apply accounting principles and International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).
Create a detailed chart of accounts tailored to the organization’s business model.
Establish clear policies and procedures for managing fixed assets.
Formulate policies for handling current assets and liabilities effectively.
Design reporting frameworks that comply with IFRS standards.
